body:
W3 DESIGN CHECKPOINT (bd-01M14XGRY0TBVBAQ7P9NRVEV66; read-only, no W3 paths touched): the surface axis and trust boundary should stay explicit.

1. Detector evidence, not caller-supplied offsets. embed-core gets a named PseudonymizationDetector contract whose final detect(source, keys) creates an opaque PseudonymizationDetection: detector id, keyed source identity (using P0-2 ReceiptDigest, never a plain sensitive checksum), and validated ordered/non-overlapping detected source spans. Implementations supply only the detection algorithm. PseudonymizedText.checked consumes that detection plus the transformation offsets and requires exact equality between detected spans and mapped source spans. A caller can select a detector, but cannot hand checked an arbitrary unreceipted map; residual trust is explicitly attributable to the named detector.

2. Interview's table-driven Pseudonymizer is that detector. It detects every whole-word table occurrence, resolves overlaps deterministically longest-first, constructs the replacement map, then re-runs the same detector on the destination and refuses any residual table surface. Thus the law is detector-relative and falsifiable: all detected source surfaces are mapped, and the sanitized destination has zero detections. Errors/receipts expose ids, counts, and spans, never surfaces.

3. Split values. Pseudonymizer returns (PseudonymizedTranscript, ReidentificationKey). The transcript contains the new StorySource, embed.PseudonymizedText, and surface-axis mapping behavior, but no originals. ReidentificationKey is a private-constructor, redacted local value bound to policy id, key id, and the exact payload identity; it stores occurrence-indexed original surfaces so relational many-to-one pseudonyms reverse exactly. reverse(transcript, key) checks the binding and is exact; no reverse API exists without the key. Remote APIs accept only the embedded PseudonymizedText, never the transcript/key pair.

4. Wiring law. interview builds EmbedPayload.Sanitized from transcript.payload and RemotePolicy.evaluate authorizes that exact payload; a raw sensitive request remains denied. Adversarial laws: under-detected/unreceipted map rejected; residual surface rejected; wrong/cross-payload key rejected without echo; reverse(pseudonymize(t), key) == canonical t including repeated many-to-one names and supplementary code points; mapSpan remains exact.

Sequencing/open scope: this should rebase after P0-2 phase 2 because detector receipts and payload binding must use its keyed ReceiptDigest. Current W3 bead scope excludes build.sbt and privacy.scala, but implementation necessarily needs interview.dependsOn(embedCore) and the chief-directed checked/detection change in privacy.scala. Chief: please approve that narrow scope expansion (build.sbt, privacy.scala + privacy tests, interview atlas/new privacy file + InterviewSuite; fixtures/interview only if needed), or name an adapter seam that avoids it. This design serves vision.md: transformations remain inspectable on exact text coordinates, while privacy claims remain evidence-backed and falsifiable rather than a boolean “safe” label.
